target.title: feat(cron): serve cron run history from the task ledger
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

One cron execution today produces three overlapping records: a rich `cron_run_logs` row, a deliberately thin `task_runs` mirror (silent, `not_applicable`, best-effort), and a session-registry row — plus dual-written `CronJobState` last-run fields. Downstream, task maintenance needs a cron-specific recovery branch that cross-reads two cron stores, and the Control UI shows the same execution twice at different fidelity (Automations run history vs Tasks page).

Part 1 of 2 for #106041: make the task ledger the authoritative record for cron executions and flip the external read paths, while keeping the legacy `cron_run_logs` dual-write as a revert safety net. PR 2 migrates old history, deletes the run-log stack, and unifies cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `task_runs` gains a generic nullable `detail_json` column (additive `ensureColumn` migration + regenerated Kysely types). Cron owns the codec ([task-run-detail.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/cron/task-run-detail.ts)) between run outcomes, ledger detail, and the **unchanged** `CronRunLogEntry` wire shape.
- Cron writes full-fidelity terminal rows (status vocabulary, delivery trace, `errorReason`, `triggerFired`, `nextRunAtMs`, model/usage) instead of the lobotomized mirror; skipped runs now create immediately-terminal rows so history parity holds.
- `cron.runs` RPC, the CLI run-history poll, and task-maintenance cron recovery read from the ledger ([task-run-history.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/cron/task-run-history.ts)); the maintenance cron branch shrinks from two cross-store readers to a ledger self-lookup, and `configureTaskRegistryMaintenance` loses its `cronStorePath` parameter.
- Startup crash recovery improves: a run that finished before the crash is restored from its finalized ledger row (with `record-only` failure-alert cooldown restore) instead of being reported as "interrupted".
- Same-millisecond executions get distinct ledger rows via a run-id discriminator; the reservation timestamp keys recovery.

- Existing history migrates automatically: a one-shot state migration ([state-migrations.cron-run-logs.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/infra/state-migrations.cron-run-logs.ts)) imports `cron_run_logs` rows into the ledger at first DB open — no manual doctor step — with deterministic import ids for idempotency and dual-write-aware duplicate matching.
- History reads stay scoped to the configured cron store: `cron_run_logs` partitions by `store_key`, so ledger detail records the store key and `readCronTaskRunHistoryPage` filters by it (kept out of the wire shape; test-locked).

Non-goals here (PR 2): stopping the dual-write, dropping `cron_run_logs` + `cron.runLog.*` config keys, per-source retention, cancel unification. No protocol schema, UI, or config changes; `CronRunLogEntrySchema` consumers (Control UI, macOS, Android) see identical responses.

## User Impact

No visible behavior change. Cron run history is served from the shared task ledger; Automations history and the Tasks page now describe the same rows. Crash-interrupted-but-completed runs report their true outcome after restart instead of a synthetic interruption error.

## Evidence

- Parity tests: ledger-served history equals legacy run-log responses across ok/error/timeout/skipped, delivery statuses, trigger, telemetry, paging, and text-query filtering (`src/cron/task-run-history.test.ts`).
- Race matrix: operator-cancel precedence, lost-row overwrite, same-ms collisions, skip rows (`src/cron/service/task-runs.test.ts`, `ops.test.ts`, `timer.test.ts`).
- Serialized-detail shape locked behind the indexed LIKE prefixes so codec field reordering fails loudly.
- **Production-data migration proof**: against a copied 247 MB production state DB (2,750 legacy run-log rows, 5 jobs, 952 pre-upgrade task rows): 2,750/2,750 imported, 0 malformed, ledger vs legacy reader totals equal and first page byte-identical, second open idempotent (no double import).
- Focused packs green locally (~1,750 tests across cron/tasks/gateway/infra surfaces); structured second-model review run to zero accepted findings (two accepted findings fixed: legacy runId recovery, store-key scoping + auto-migration); full gates on hosted CI/Testbox.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Test evidence (post-rebase, Node v22.19.0)**:

Runtime tests — all 5 new tests pass:
```console
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=completed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=failed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=aborted, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ keeps the lane when terminal-phase reply operation is still within the settle window
 ✓ reclaims no-progress reply operations (phase=running, phantom without diagnostic activity)
 ✓ (25 more pre-existing tests pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed | 1 failed (31)
```
The single failure (`logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`) is a pre-existing SQLite version issue (Node 22.19.0 embeds SQLite 3.50.4; OpenClaw requires 22.22.3+) — unrelated to this PR.

**E2E reclaim proof** — real gateway components + real `diag.warn()` terminal output:

```console
=== failed (retainFailureUntilComplete) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-failed sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s queueDepth=1 activeSessionId=e2e-failed-session phase=failed
stuck session recovery: sessionId=e2e-failed-session sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=0
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0
→ Queued message: drained

=== aborted (running → abortByUser) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-aborted ... phase=aborted
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

=== completed (setPhase, no complete()) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-completed ... phase=completed
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The diagnostic warnings (`diag.warn()` calls inside `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`) are captured directly and printed as terminal output — no mocks, no assertions-only. This is the exact log output that a running gateway produces when it reclaims a terminal-phase phantom.

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 30/31 passed (1 pre-existing SQLite env failure)
integration tests: 10/10 passed (was 7)
Total: 40/41 passed across 2 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

Related to #105712

target.title: feat(mcp): requester-scoped MCP server connections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106229. In multi-user channels (Slack workspaces, group chats), every sender shares one MCP connection set: MCP servers come only from static config/bundle manifests and runtimes are cached per `sessionId`. Per-user-credentialed MCP (hosted providers minting one MCP session per end user — e.g. per-user OAuth email/calendar) is impossible: one user's authenticated session would leak to everyone in the thread, or the integration cannot exist at all. A conversation session is not an authorization boundary — a Slack thread has many senders.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a generic, provider-agnostic core primitive; all provider logic stays in plugins:

- **New plugin API:** `api.registerMcpServerConnectionResolver({ serverName, resolve })`. Server *identity* stays static (`mcp.servers` / bundle manifest: name, tool filter); only the *connection* (`url`/`headers`) is resolved per trusted requester. `resolve(ctx)` receives runtime-provided trusted identity (`requesterSenderId`, `agentAccountId`, `messageChannel`); returning `null` omits the server for that run.
- **Requester-keyed runtimes:** requester-scoped servers get runtimes keyed `(sessionId, messageChannel, agentAccountId, requesterSenderId)`; static servers keep the existing per-session lifecycle byte-for-byte. Sessions with no registered resolvers are entirely unchanged.
- **Fail closed:** runs without a trusted `requesterSenderId` (cron, subagent, heartbeat) never materialize requester-scoped servers; there is no shared-connection fallback. `senderId` is populated only from the verified inbound envelope (invariant documented at the seam in `attempt.ts`).
- **Credential hygiene:** resolved `url`/`headers` never enter config fingerprints, logs, catalog descriptions, or persisted state. Rotation detection uses an ephemeral per-process HMAC digest (nothing derivable offline). Resolver failures/timeouts log fixed classifications only — no plugin-controlled text.
- **Lifecycle:** per-key serialized resolve+install (promise-chain mutex — no interleaving race class), bounded 10s resolver timeout, 5-minute credential revalidation with rebuild-on-rotation, revocation disposes cached transports even under lease (authorization boundary), idle-TTL sweep covers all keys.
- **Prompt-cache stability:** tool names/schemas are requester-independent; safe-name assignment derives deterministically from the full declared server set regardless of which connections resolve.

Precedent: the plugin tool descriptor cache already keys on `requesterSenderId`; this extends the established pattern to MCP transports. The API surface intentionally leaves room for a future cron/subagent user-context fix (#102098) to flow through additively.

**Note for reviewers (surface changes):** no new `openclaw.json` keys or env vars. Plugin SDK gains one registration method + 3 public type exports; `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` public-exports budget bumped 10645 → 10648 to match (commented in the diff). `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` regenerated per the check's documented flow.

## User Impact

Operators can install plugins that give each trusted channel user their own authenticated MCP-backed tools (email, calendar, CRM) in shared channels. Sender B's run can never invoke sender A's transport — the capability is not attached to B's run. Existing configurations see zero behavior change. Known and documented: content one user's tools place into a shared thread remains visible in that thread's transcript (group-chat semantics; private queries belong in DM sessions).

## Evidence

- Issue with full design rationale: #106229 (links #102098, #72591/#92221, #79451).
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox + local focused runs): `pnpm check:changed` lanes green (format, SDK baseline, SDK exports, surface budget, lint); `tsgo` + `tsgo:test` exit 0; focused suites `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `mcp-connection-resolver`, `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize`, `agent-bundle-mcp-names`, `agent-bundle-mcp-filter` — 100+ tests green.
- Six rounds of structured adversarial review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) drove the hardening above: resolver timeout/error containment, revocation-disposes-under-lease, per-key serialization replacing three interim concurrency guards (net −70 LOC in the manager), HMAC digest instead of plain credential hash, constant catalog descriptions, SSE alias preservation, lease aggregation for requester-only sessions, safe-name-map fingerprint participation.
- Tests cover: per-sender runtime keying with static sharing, fail-closed paths (no requester / resolver null / resolver throw / resolver timeout), fingerprint stability under alternating senders, credential rotation rebuild + revocation disposal, out-of-order concurrent resolution, dispose-during-resolve, requester-only lease preservation, cross-partition safe-name determinism, no credential material in fingerprints/logs/catalog summaries.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: gateway MCP-app reconstruction lacks requester context (scoped servers stay fail-closed absent there); cron/subagent requester context is #102098.

Written with AI assistance; reviewed and directed by @obviyus.

target.title: fix(infra): use Buffer.byteLength for JSON string byte-limit fast-path guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`jsonStringByteLengthUpToLimit` in `src/infra/json-utf8-bytes.ts` uses `value.length` (UTF-16 code unit count) as a fast-path estimate of JSON-encoded byte size. For CJK text this underestimates the actual UTF-8 byte count by up to **3×** — `"中".repeat(100)` has `.length = 100` but `Buffer.byteLength = 300`.

The guard `value.length + 2 > remainingBytes` is meant to bail early when a string definitely won't fit in the remaining budget, avoiding the expensive `JSON.stringify` + `Buffer.byteLength` fallback. With CJK content, this guard incorrectly passes strings that should bail, wasting an allocation on every miss.

The accurate fallback (`jsonUtf8BytesOrInfinity`) still catches the overflow, so **no data corruption occurs**. But each miss triggers an unnecessary `JSON.stringify` allocation that the fast path was designed to prevent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `value.length` with `Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8")`. `Buffer.byteLength` on a string is O(n) without allocating a buffer — still much cheaper than the `JSON.stringify` fallback it guards against.

`Buffer.byteLength` is already used elsewhere in the same file (lines 4, 6, 23), and the `+ 2` JSON-quote constant is preserved.

## User Impact

- `boundedJsonUtf8Bytes` fast-path bailout now works correctly for CJK and emoji content
- No behaviour change for ASCII text (`byteLength == length`)
- Callers unaffected: `session-tool-result-guard`, `worker-environments/inference`, `tool-result-middleware` — all 105 caller tests pass

## Evidence

**Environment**: Node.js v24.13.1, Linux x86_64, upstream/main at e9e62b563.

**Scenario**: `boundedJsonUtf8Bytes({value: "中".repeat(100)}, 200)` — the object is 302 JSON bytes, but the budget is only 200. The fast path should bail early:

```bash
node --import tsx -e '
import { Buffer } from "node:buffer";
const value = "中".repeat(100);
const remainingBytes = 190;  // after object framing overhead
// old guard
const oldBail = value.length + 2 > remainingBytes;
// new guard
const newBail = Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8") + 2 > remainingBytes;
console.log("value:", value.length, "code units,", Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8"), "UTF-8 bytes");
console.log("JSON actual:", Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(value), "utf8"), "bytes");
console.log("budget:", remainingBytes, "bytes remaining");
console.log("old guard (length + 2):", value.length + 2, ">", remainingBytes, "=", oldBail);
console.log("new guard (byteLength + 2):", Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8") + 2, ">", remainingBytes, "=", newBail);
'
```

```
value: 100 code units, 300 UTF-8 bytes
JSON actual: 302 bytes
budget: 190 bytes remaining
old guard (length + 2): 102 > 190 = false   ← missed bailout: does unnecessary JSON.stringify
new guard (byteLength + 2): 302 > 190 = true  ← correct bailout
```

**Regression — ASCII unchanged** (all 3 scenarios agree):

```
短 ASCII: old=false new=false actual=7 limit=10   agree ✅
长 ASCII: old=true  new=true  actual=502 limit=100 agree ✅
emoji:    old=true  new=true  actual=202 limit=50  agree ✅
```

**Unit tests**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/json-utf8-bytes.test.ts \
  src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/inference.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  6 passed (6)
```

target.title: fix(reply): use document cap for local media attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refs #40880 for the Telegram outbound reply-media path.

Telegram can send generated local documents larger than 5 MiB, but final-reply media staging was dropping an unconfigured 23,456,667 byte PPTX before it reached Telegram `sendDocument`. Direct Telegram `sendDocument` for the same file succeeded, so the failing boundary was local reply-media staging rather than the Telegram adapter or the PPTX MIME type.

## Summary

Local final-reply attachments sent back to Telegram now use the document media cap when no explicit `mediaMaxMb` is configured.

## Change

- Preserve explicit channel/account/default `mediaMaxMb` overrides.
- Use the 100 MiB document cap only for unconfigured Telegram reply-media staging.
- Keep unconfigured non-Telegram reply-media staging on the existing 5 MiB media-store cap.
- Add focused tests for the Telegram default cap and the non-Telegram fallback.

## Evidence

Real failure observed on a Telegram reply with:

- `MEDIA:./tmp/izen_shooting/Annual_CIS_Conference_2026_RU.pptx`
- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`
- `23,456,667` bytes

Focused validation after this patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.final-media-runreplyagent.test.ts
# 2 files passed, 26 tests passed
```

Live Telegram smoke proof from a real OpenClaw Telegram reply:

![Redacted Telegram screenshot showing an 8.0 MB PPTX delivered without Media failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-99189-proof-assets/proofs/pr-99189/telegram-pptx-8mb-proof-redacted.jpg)

- File shown by Telegram: `test_local_reply_media_8mb_...pptx`
- Telegram UI size/type: `8.0 MB PPTX`
- Result: the document is visible in Telegram without `Media failed`

Telegram limit note: the cloud Bot API upload limit is 50 MB for documents, while a self-hosted local Bot API server supports uploads up to 2000 MB. This proof intentionally stays inside the normal cloud `sendDocument` envelope while crossing the old 5 MiB reply-media staging cap.

target.title: fix(chat): preserve explicit current-source sends in Control UI history
target.body:
Related: #104544
Related: #83494

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could explicitly send a successful `message` tool reply to the exact current source conversation, while Control UI history omitted that delivered reply and showed only a later, different assistant final.

This PR addresses the explicit current-source `message` send slice of #104544. It does not address missing subagent lifecycle announcements, which are tracked separately in #105517.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit routes were excluded from message-tool history projection even when the resolved channel, account, target, and thread matched the current source conversation. The change adds a structured current-source route marker at the outbound owner and permits marker-backed successful explicit sends in the history projector.

Dry-run, suppressed, and explicit `ok: false` results remain excluded. Existing transcript delivery mirrors remain authoritative and are deduplicated.

## User Impact

Users who receive an explicit agent reply in the current Telegram/Slack source conversation can now see the same reply in Control UI session history. Later assistant output no longer replaces that delivered message in the dashboard.

Cross-channel, cross-account, cross-target, and cross-thread sends remain excluded from the current session history.

## Evidence

- Exact patch head: `ccceb3f971e24022effe1b170a217edf618761ff`
- Exact replay base: `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`
- Current exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29249860500 (passed)
- Current exact-head fork patch CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29249860584 (passed)
- Current upstream PR CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29249852157 (passed)
- Previous exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29246179834 (passed at `f89cdc7b510268a9cd76c7e66c44784f8afe4bc7`)
- Previous exact-head upstream PR CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29242075130 (passed at `5ca0701495e263fe78a784d270ca7d154ecdcfe4`)

The branch was replayed without patch-content changes onto upstream `main` at `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`. A commit-by-commit range comparison matched all seven patch commits. The prior exact-head failures reproduced on the corresponding upstream baseline and were outside this PR's nine changed files: dangling msteams symbols, generated locale inventory drift, a plugin SDK baseline hash, and an asynchronous SQLite reliability helper mismatch. All of those upstream failures are repaired in this replay base. Upstream `main` has since advanced only in files outside this PR's nine-file surface, so another replay is not needed for this evidence cycle.

The exact-head Control UI workflow passed and produced the expected artifact. Upstream PR CI and fork patch CI also passed against the refreshed patch: the upstream workflow tested the merge result, while the fork workflow pinned the exact patch SHA.

## Risk And Rollback

Risk is limited to read-time history projection and the structured result metadata used to prove an exact current-source route. The marker is emitted only after trusted channel/account/target/thread resolution, and projection continues to reject existing non-success indicators.

Rollback is a straight revert of this PR. No config, schema, transcript migration, or persisted data rewrite is introduced.

## Documentation

No documentation change is needed. This restores consistency between an existing channel delivery path and the existing Control UI history surface without changing configuration or user-facing commands.

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Unit test**: `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["fs.listDir"])` now returns `["operator.pairing", "operator.admin"]`

```
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts (6 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Integration test**: Full `node.pair.approve` RPC flow via gateway — 12 existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression to `system.run`, `browser.proxy`, or non-admin command approval paths.

```
✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts (12 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
```

- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` passes without errors.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `operator.write` (non-admin) operator can approve a node advertising the `fs.listDir` capability, whereas invoking `fs.listDir` requires `operator.admin`; the fix makes approval require `operator.admin` too.

Real environment tested: drove the real `approveNodePairing` reducer through its on-disk paired-device store in a fresh temp directory — the real `requestDevicePairing`, `approveDevicePairing`, `requestNodePairing`, `approveNodePairing`, and `resolveMissingRequestedScope` all ran against the real SQLite store, with nothing stubbed (the store was seeded through the real pairing request/approve functions).

Exact steps run after this patch: seed a paired node device, request a node surface declaring `commands: ["fs.listDir"]`, then call `approveNodePairing(requestId, { callerScopes: ["operator.pairing", "operator.write"] }, baseDir)` and record the returned outcome.

Evidence after fix:

```
caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.write]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> FORBIDDEN missingScope=operator.admin

caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.admin]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> APPROVED requestId=0795d316-6191-4d0c-ad8c-a723cb962e00
persisted commands: ["fs.listDir"]
```

## Reviewer Notes

Codex's review notes that the two admin-command classifications
(`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` and `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS`) are
independently maintained, which has now caused two authorization mismatches
(#104491 for `browser.proxy`, this PR for `fs.listDir`).

This concern is well understood. However, the two lists are not identical by
design: `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` includes `system.run.*` (which requires
admin at approval time but not at invoke time, since `system.run` is already
protected by agent-layer `BLOCKED_INVOKE_COMMANDS` and descriptor-level scope
alignment), while `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` does not. A single shared
constant would either over-approximate one side or lose this semantic
distinction.

For this P1 security fix, I've kept the change minimal — the same pattern that

target.title: fix(http-error-body): log response body snippet read errors instead of silently returning empty string
target.body:
## Summary

`readResponseBodySnippet` used a bare `catch {}` that silently swallowed all errors and returned `""` with no diagnostic. This PR replaces it with `catch (err) { errorBodyLog.warn(...); return ""; }` so failures are visible in diagnostics.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/infra/http-error-body.ts:25`, `readResponseBodySnippet` catches all errors and returns an empty string with no logging. When a response body cannot be read — network failure, body already consumed, stream abort, decode error — the failure is completely invisible. Callers receive `""` and cannot distinguish between a genuinely empty response body and a read failure.

**Code evidence**: In `http-error-body.ts:25`, the `catch { return ""; }` provides zero visibility into why the snippet read failed.

## Root Cause

The function was written with best-effort semantics (it provides a diagnostic snippet, not the primary response data), but the empty catch block went too far by discarding all diagnostic information. Similar to the pattern fixed in [#106385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106385).

## Why This Fix

Follows the same pattern accepted in:
- [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) (`fix(delivery): log failDelivery errors instead of silently swallowing`) by @SebTardif
- [#106385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106385) (`fix(restart-sentinel): log DB errors instead of silently swallowing them`)

Uses `createSubsystemLogger("http-error-body")` + `formatErrorMessage(err)` — consistent with other infra modules.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Operators had no diagnostic signal when an HTTP error body snippet could not be read — failures were completely invisible.
- **After**: A warning is emitted (`[http-error-body]` prefix) with the full error context; the function continues to return `""` (safe default for diagnostic snippets).

## Evidence

- **Before**: No warnings emitted when `response.text()` rejects — error is silently swallowed.
- **After**: Warning emitted with full error context; empty string returned as safe default.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
=== readResponseBodySnippet (error case) ===
Returned: ""
readResponseBodySnippet completed without throwing

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
      The catch block is silently swallowing errors.
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
=== readResponseBodySnippet (error case) ===
Returned: ""
readResponseBodySnippet completed without throwing

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
PASS: Warning was emitted on stderr:
  [http-error-body] Failed to read response body snippet: body already consumed
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed (no lint errors)
- Added 2 regression tests: `response.text()` rejection + stream abort

target.title: fix(restart-sentinel): log DB errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## Summary

`clearRestartSentinel`, `readRestartSentinel`, and `hasRestartSentinel` used empty `catch {}` / `catch { return null }` / `catch { return false }` blocks that silently swallowed SQLite DB errors. This PR replaces them with `sentinelLog.warn(...)` so errors are visible in diagnostics while preserving the best-effort semantics.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, three exported functions silently discard all errors from the SQLite state database:

- **`clearRestartSentinel`** — `catch {}`: If the DB write fails (locked, corrupt, disk full), the sentinel is not cleared but the caller has no way to detect this. The gateway may continue to believe a restart is pending.
- **`readRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return null }`: Any DB read error (transient lock, corruption) is treated identically to "no sentinel exists", potentially causing a pending restart to be silently dropped.
- **`hasRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return false }`: Same problem — DB errors are indistinguishable from "no sentinel".

**Code evidence**: In `restart-sentinel.ts:228`, the `catch {}` on the `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` call provides no visibility into whether the sentinel was actually cleared.

## Root Cause

The functions were written with best-effort semantics (they must not throw during shutdown/cleanup), but the empty catch blocks went too far by discarding all diagnostic information. Unlike the intentional best-effort pattern in `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` (which includes a comment explaining why the catch is empty), these catch blocks had no explanation and no logging.

## Why This Fix

Follows the same pattern accepted in:
- [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) (`fix(delivery): log failDelivery errors instead of silently swallowing`) by @SebTardif
- [#82943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82943) (`fix(agents): log warnings instead of swallowing subagent errors`) by @SebTardif

Uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart-sentinel")` + `formatErrorMessage(err)` — consistent with `restart.ts` which also uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart")`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Operators had no diagnostic signal when the restart sentinel could not be cleared or read — failures were completely invisible.
- **After**: A warning is emitted to the diagnostics log (`[restart-sentinel]` prefix) with the full error context, while the functions continue to return safe defaults (`null` / `false` / `undefined`).

## Evidence

- **Before**: No warnings emitted on stderr when the DB operation fails — errors are silently swallowed.
- **After**: Three warnings emitted with full error context; functions return safely without throwing.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main, `catch {}`)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
      The catch blocks are silently swallowing errors.
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
PASS: Warnings were emitted on stderr:
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to clear restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to read restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to check restart sentinel: ...
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed (no lint errors)
- Added 3 regression tests in `restart-sentinel.test.ts` verifying that each function survives DB failures without throwing and returns the safe default value

target.title: fix(oauth): make getOAuthApiKey refresh within the standard margin (issue #103846)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getOAuthApiKey` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` decided whether to refresh an OAuth token using a raw expiry check (`Date.now() >= creds.expires`). The OAuth manager gate, `hasUsableOAuthCredential` (`src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-state.ts`), decides refresh using a 5-minute margin (`DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS`).

When a credential was inside the margin window but not yet past its raw expiry, the manager correctly decided a refresh was needed, took the global refresh lock, and delegated to `getOAuthApiKey` — but `getOAuthApiKey` saw `now < expires` and **skipped the refresh silently**, returning the unchanged credential as if the refresh succeeded. The caller then used a stale token until raw expiry, instead of refreshing early.

## Evidence

- `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts:105` used `if (Date.now() >= creds.expires)` (raw expiry).
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-state.ts:54` `hasUsableOAuthCredential` uses `resolveTokenExpiryState(..., { expiringWithinMs: refreshMarginMs })` with `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000`.
- Callers `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts:213` and `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts:466` are refresh paths that expect margin-aware refresh; neither relied on the old raw-expiry skip.
- New regression test `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.test.ts` covers the margin window (4 min remaining → refresh fires), comfortably-outside (30 min → no refresh), and past-expiry (→ refresh fires).

## Fix

Replaced the raw `Date.now() >= creds.expires` check with the shared `hasUsableOAuthCredential(creds)`, so the low-level delegate uses the same margin as the manager gate. One import, one condition. No behavior change for the two existing callers other than the intended early-refresh.

## Runtime Proof

`scripts/proof-oauth-margin.mjs` mirrors the exact decision functions from `credential-state.ts` (`resolveTokenExpiryState`, `hasUsableOAuthCredential`) and the old/new `getOAuthApiKey` gates, then runs a credential 2 minutes from expiry (inside the 5-minute margin):

```text
$ node scripts/proof-oauth-margin.mjs
MARGIN_MS=300000
creds.expires - now = 120000 ms (inside margin)
hasUsableOAuthCredential = false (manager gate: REFRESH)
OLD getOAuthApiKey refresh? false  -> returns unchanged creds (STALE TOKEN)
NEW getOAuthApiKey refresh? true  -> refreshes within margin (FRESH TOKEN)

RESULT: PASS — within margin, OLD skipped refresh (bug) but NEW refreshes (fixed)
```

The same margin window is covered by the committed regression test `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.test.ts` (no real Anthropic credentials needed).

Closes #103846

target.title: fix(zalo): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo recipients could see internal assistant tool-failure banners or raw tool-call XML instead of only the user-visible response.

Related: #90684

## Why This Change Was Made

Zalo now opts into the existing shared assistant-visible-text sanitizer through the standard channel outbound `sanitizeText` hook. Core applies this hook before payload normalization, empty filtering, chunk planning, and the current attached-result Zalo transport adapter.

The branch was rebased onto current `main` and retains the newer `sendZaloDelivery`, `zaloSendResultAdapter`, and `createAttachedChannelResultAdapter` flow; no deprecated send-result path is restored.

## User Impact

Zalo users receive the intended assistant prose without internal tool traces or XML scaffolding. Ordinary messages are unchanged, and trace-only text is removed before outbound chunking and delivery.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Zalo's outbound adapter did not declare the shared assistant-visible-text sanitizer, allowing internal failed-tool banners and tool XML to reach channel delivery.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.14, original branch `fix/zalo-outbound-tool-trace-sanitize`, exact head `66dfdda620f9d0156ff3a621501910d198346503`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `370b5150c25961d6b46c32829b5f44a3a9b60557`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node --import tsx` with a runtime harness importing `zaloPlugin` from `extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts` and invoking the actual outbound `sanitizeText` hook for mixed, XML, ordinary, and trace-only payloads.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  mixed: PASS output="Done."
  xml: PASS output="Message sent."
  ordinary: PASS output="The group has 5 active members."
  trace-only: PASS output=""
  ALL PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Mixed visible/trace content retains only visible prose, tool-call XML is removed, ordinary prose is byte-equivalent, and trace-only input becomes empty before core's empty-payload suppression and transport delivery.

The shared final-delivery pass and the channel delivery profile were also compared directly on the current base. The shared `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` pass is intentionally conservative and leaves all four reported Zalo payload classes unchanged; `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` removes them:

```text
banner shared="Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
banner delivery="Done."
tool-call shared="<tool_call>{\"name\":\"exec\"}</tool_call>Message sent."

function-response delivery="Checking now.\n\nMessage sent."

```

This establishes that the Zalo hook is the existing channel-owned full delivery profile layered after core's conservative runtime-marker pass, not a duplicate implementation of the same sanitizer.
- **What was not tested:** A live Zalo Bot API round trip. The actual rebased adapter hook, current payload/transport contracts, shared sanitizer semantics, and core delivery pipeline were exercised without Zalo credentials. target.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code catalog sessions on paired nodes were view-only: `continueClaudeSession` rejected any `hostId` other than `gateway:local`, so a session whose files live on another machine could be browsed but never continued. Closes #105529.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuing a Claude session must run the real `claude` CLI on the machine that owns the session files (its `~/.claude`, its auth) — OpenClaw stays a frontend and never substitutes its own inference. This PR ships the full TS stack for that, opt-in and approval-gated end to end:

- **Streaming node invoke (additive transport)**: new `node.invoke.progress` events (`{invokeId, nodeId, seq, chunk}`) with strict seq ordering, bounded out-of-order buffering, idle-timeout reset on progress, hard-cap timeout, and `node.invoke.cancel`. Legacy single-result invokes stay byte-identical (cancel frames are gated to streaming invokes). Progress handlers are node-scoped and bind invokeId to the owning node's connection — no cross-node injection.
- **Node command `agent.cli.claude.run.v1`** (TS node host): advertised only when the node-local config `nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled` is true AND the `claude` binary resolves on the node — the gateway can never force it on. Requests are validated against a strict Claude flag allowlist (`bypassPermissions` rejected in both arg forms), env passthrough is allowlisted, cwd must exist, and every run flows through the existing `system.run` exec-approval policy with the exact validated argv. Output is capped (200KB, 16KB chunks with backpressure), stderr tailed, process tree SIGKILLed on cancel/timeout, and the system prompt is materialized in a node-local 0600 temp file that is always cleaned up.
- **cli-runner placement branch**: sessions with `execHost === "node"` run one-shot `claude -p` turns through the streaming invoke, feeding the same JSONL parser as local runs (session-id capture, fork markers, tool events unchanged). Warm stdio, gateway-loopback MCP, skills dirs, reseed-from-transcript, and attachments are cleanly disabled for node runs (rejected or omitted, double-enforced by the node-side allowlist); local runs are byte-identical.
- **Catalog wiring**: node rows become continuable when the node advertises the run command AND the gateway's node command policy permits it (deny-wins, enforced at projection, continue, and invoke time). Adoption re-resolves the record from the node itself (client-supplied paths never trusted), imports bounded history via the existing read command, and binds the session with `execNode`/`execCwd` through the trusted creation seam. First-turn `--fork-session` semantics identical to local adoption.

Mac-app (Swift) nodes simply never advertise the command and remain view-only until the app ships it.

## User Impact

With a headless node host opted in (`nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled: true` + `claude` installed), Claude Code sessions on that machine appear in the session catalog and can be continued like native sessions: each turn runs on the node with the node's Claude auth and settings, streams output live, and respects the node's exec approval policy. Nothing changes for nodes that do not opt in; existing node/gateway deployments see zero wire-format changes.

## Evidence

- Focused matrix green post-rebase (8 Vitest shards): node-registry transport ordering/idle/disconnect, node-host argv-validation/approval/caps/cancel, cli-runner placement/JSONL-across-chunks/fork/deadline-during-approval, config contract, plugin runtime projection, catalog adoption/rejection paths.
- Codex-side validation on Linux Testbox: 12 test files (574 executions), `check:changed` (12m21s), `pnpm build` — all green pre-review.
- Three independent deep reviews (transport, cli-runner placement, catalog/config/plugin seams): all SOLID, zero P1s. The one P2 (hard-timeout previously emitted `node.invoke.cancel` for legacy invokes too) is fixed — cancel frames now gate on the streaming contract.
- Per-commit autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) surfaced five findings, all fixed with regression tests: buffered progress no longer drains after cancellation; duplicate buffered seq frames no longer reset the idle deadline; node runs now carry the gateway's native tool policy (`--tools` + MCP deny projected; `--allowedTools` auto-approval still never crosses the node boundary); fresh node CLI sessions reseed conversation history from the gateway-side transcript; and a truncated node stream that lost the terminal result line now fails the turn instead of passing as a clean exit.
- SDK gates: `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (surface budget +1 for `resolveChildProcessInvocation`, now public via the `process-runtime` wildcard — needed by the node host for Windows shim-correct spawns).
- tsgo core + UI lanes green; oxlint/oxfmt/`git diff --check` clean.

Known follow-ups (deliberate v1 scope, in the tracking issue): Mac-app Swift command, warm stdio on nodes, gateway-loopback MCP over node transport, Codex app-server on nodes, approval-request withdrawal when a run aborts mid-wait, FailoverError classification for node disconnects.

## What Problem This Solves

The web Control UI can manage scheduled gateway work, while the native mobile apps exposed only a partial cron surface. iOS lacked safe detail/edit/history/run/delete controls, and both mobile platforms lacked practical search and status filtering.

Closes #106145.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use the existing `cron.*` gateway contract; no new protocol or config surface.
- Add mobile-appropriate management parity while keeping creation, cloning, and dense delivery/failure-routing editing in the Control UI.
- Preserve optimistic-concurrency safety with `expectedConfigRevision` and fail closed when the connected gateway changes.
- Track queued runs by exact `runId`, paginate the complete automation list, and preserve unsaved drafts.
- Fold in the outstanding native Skills review fixes from #105814.

## User Impact

- iOS and Android now call the feature **Automations**.
- Both apps support search plus All / Active / Paused filters.
- iOS adds configuration detail, recent history, revision-safe editing, enable/pause, Run Now tracking, and confirmed deletion.
- Android retains its existing management surface with the same product naming and discovery controls.
- Create/clone and advanced delivery/failure routing remain available in the web Control UI.

## Evidence

- Android focused unit tests: Cron management/runtime, Settings filters, and Skills management.
- iOS focused tests: 10 Automations model/revision/pagination/outcome tests passed on iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5.

target.title: fix(security): bound mcporter registry read in audit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readGlobalMcporterRegistrySummary` in `src/security/audit.ts` read the global MCP registry (`stateDir/skills/config/mcporter.json`) with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, so a maliciously large or corrupted registry could exhaust memory during a security audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded read with `readRegularFile`, which rejects symlinks and non-files and supports a byte cap. A 16 MiB limit is consistent with other bounded config reads in the codebase. If the file exceeds the limit or cannot be read, the function returns `null`, treating the oversized registry the same as a missing one.

## User Impact

Security audit no longer buffers an unbounded registry file into memory; behavior is unchanged for normal-sized registries.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a `16 MiB + 1` byte `mcporter.json` and asserts the `tools.exec.agent_skill_mcp_boundary_drift` finding is not emitted.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-config-basics.test.ts --run` passes (8/8 tests).

target.title: Persist gateway restart audit events
target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve opening text on rich fallback retries
target.body:
Fixes #91383.
Refs #93059.

This replaces the stalled draft #93059 on current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users could receive a corrupted plain fallback reply when a rich/HTML parse failure happened near early Markdown links, causing the delivered message to start after the assistant reply's opening text.

The affected surface is Telegram text delivery, including the ordinary reply path and the durable send path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rich parse-error fallback now carries a source-derived plain fallback through the Telegram rich chunk plan and uses that source chunk for parse-error retries instead of rebuilding fallback text from rendered rich HTML. The existing rendered-HTML fallback remains for rich entity validation cases so table-aware invalid-entity degradation keeps its current behavior.

The replacement also preserves the retry context on the plain fallback paths: link previews, silent sends, thread/reply parameters, and reply markup remain attached when Telegram rejects rich parsing.

## User Impact

Telegram replies that begin with prose and early Markdown links should keep their opening text when OpenClaw has to retry as plain text after a rich parse failure. Users with link previews disabled should keep that preference on the fallback retry as well.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(device-pair): bound notifier polling overlap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a slow device-pair notification poll could overlap later 10-second ticks and race notification state or send duplicate pairing reminders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notifier now keeps one service-lifetime poll in flight and skips interval ticks until it settles. The guard releases after success or failure, while initial polling, delivery behavior, cadence, and stop semantics remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive duplicate pairing notifications because one slow delivery crossed a polling interval, and polling resumes normally after the pending work settles.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/device-pair/notify.test.ts` on Node 24.18.0: 3 tests passed.
- Regression coverage advances multiple intervals while a poll is deferred, verifies stop/start does not overlap it, and proves polling resumes after both resolution and rejection.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.

## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled notifier lifecycle proof

- Base commit: `a5c5e3b713e7c16225394196af2cb37413f6fe22`.
- Exact PR head: `f8baa416e8fb70617042976cc70fdb1d6cf45e1e`.
- Scope: the committed regression test invokes the production `createPairingNotifierService().start()/stop()` lifecycle. It replaces only the device-pair listing boundary, uses the repository plugin-state test runtime, and drives the production 10-second interval with fake timers.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/device-pair/notify.test.ts --reporter verbose
  ```

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  PASS device-pair notify persistence > skips interval ticks while a notify poll is pending and resumes after it settles
  ```

- Observation: the production service made one initial poll and one interval poll. While that second poll remained pending, two more interval ticks and a stop/start cycle started no additional poll. After settlement, the next tick started one poll; two more ticks while that poll was pending again started none. Rejection released the guard, and the following tick resumed polling. The focused test also retained the existing subscriber persistence coverage.
- Not tested: live Telegram delivery, a real device-pair request, a full Gateway process, or wall-clock waiting. target.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where timed-out Discord event listeners continued running after the queue released their concurrency slots, allowing actual listener work to exceed the configured `maxConcurrency`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each listener now starts once, still resolves its dispatch through the existing timeout path, and retains its accounting slot until the uncancellable listener promise actually settles. Late failures remain consumed, timeout metrics remain intact, and the existing bounded pending queue remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Discord gateway workloads now honor the configured listener concurrency bound even when handlers outlive their timeout, preventing timeout bursts from creating uncontrolled background concurrency.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/client.test.ts` on Node 24.18.0: 20 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves a queued listener does not start after the first listener times out, then starts exactly once after the underlying promise settles.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.

## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Discord gateway queue proof

- Base commit: `b76a7f453bd48e686d4e97f22e39c75ffad7818f`.
- Exact PR head: `9cf481015fe27564c74ad09ec92c4ce94ccf3ee5`.
- Scope: the committed regression tests invoke the production Discord `Client.dispatchGatewayEvent()` and `DiscordEventQueue` paths. Listener bodies are controlled deferred promises, while queueing, timeout dispatch, metrics, slot accounting, and late-settlement handling remain production code.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/client.test.ts --reporter verbose
  ```

- Transcript:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  PASS Client gateway event queue > resolves timed-out dispatches while retaining the hung listener slot
  PASS Client gateway event queue > holds a timed-out listener slot until its underlying promise settles
  PASS Client gateway event queue > limits queued listener concurrency
  PASS Client gateway event queue > rejects when queued listener work exceeds maxQueueSize
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       20 passed (20)
  ```

- Observation: with `listenerTimeout=10ms` and `maxConcurrency=1`, the first dispatch settled through the existing timeout path and incremented the timeout/processed metrics, but the second listener remained queued and `processing` stayed at one. Rejecting the late first listener released the slot, started the second listener exactly once, consumed the late rejection, and drained the queue without increasing the logged error count.
- Not tested: a live Discord gateway connection, real Discord events, external listener I/O, or the default 120-second wall-clock timeout. Listener promises and timers are controlled, so this proves production queue timeout, slot accounting, metrics, and recovery behavior. Crabbox was unavailable in this environment; hosted fork CI provides the separate exact-head repository validation.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate run on critical tool-loop veto
target.body:
Closes #106231

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with loop detection enabled would keep burning model tokens for hours after a critical tool-loop block when the agent repeatedly called the same tool (for example `exec`) with identical arguments and outcomes. Loop detection correctly logged `action=block`, but the agent run continued until a manual `/stop`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Critical tool-loop vetoes now return a blocked tool result with agent-core’s existing `terminate: true` early-stop hint, so the current tool batch ends the run instead of only denying the next tool execution. Plugin and approval vetoes stay non-terminating. Docs describe the terminate-on-critical behavior. No new config, no independent abort path inside the detector.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — reuses agent-core terminate semantics; performance — stops unbounded post-block model calls; usability — critical loop ends the run with the existing CRITICAL reason text; security — no trust-boundary change, only enforces the safety breaker as labeled.

## User Impact

When loop detection reaches a critical threshold, OpenClaw blocks the looping tool **and** ends the agent run so the model cannot keep retrying the blocked call. Warning thresholds and post-compaction guard behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts
# 2 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts
# 83 passed (critical tool-loop blocks assert terminate: true)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts \
  -t "stops after a tool result only when the finalized result explicitly terminates|stops after a mixed tool batch when any finalized result terminates"
# 2 passed
# Mixed-batch proof: turn stays 1; both tools execute (read + exec); agent_end with no second model turn

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "tool termination|abort"
# 12 passed | 14 skipped

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts \
  packages/agent-core/src/types.ts \
  packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts \
  docs/tools/loop-detection.md
# All matched files use the correct format

git diff --check
# clean
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Critical tool-loop `action=block` must terminate the agent run so the model cannot keep issuing the same blocked tool after the safety breaker fires (issue #106231), including when the same assistant turn mixes a critical veto with a successful non-terminating tool result.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at branch `fix/106231-critical-tool-loop-terminate-run`, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, critical tool-loop blocks did not set `terminate`, and agent-core only stopped a tool batch when every finalized result terminated. A mixed batch (critical veto + success) therefore requested another model turn, matching production logs where `action=block` repeated for hours until `/stop`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts` (critical poll/generic/ping-pong paths assert `terminate: true`)
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "stops after a mixed tool batch when any finalized result terminates"`
- Evidence after fix (redacted agent-loop transcript from the mixed-batch regression):
  - Assistant turn emits two tool calls: `read` (success, no terminate) + `exec` (critical tool-loop shape with `terminate: true` / `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`).
  - Both tools finalize (`tool_execution_start` x2, `tool_execution_end` x2; executed order `["read", "exec"]`).
  - Model turn count stays `1` (second model invocation would throw `model was called after mixed-batch terminate`).
  - Stream ends with `agent_end` — run is terminal after the mixed batch.
  - Single-tool critical path still sets `terminate: true` on the blocked result only for `deniedReason === "tool-loop"`; plugin/approval vetoes remain non-terminating.
- Control check: Plugin-before-tool-call and plugin-approval blocked results omit `terminate`. Non-critical warning thresholds are unchanged. Docs state that a critical veto ends the run after the current batch even when sibling results are non-terminating.
- Observed result after fix: Focused unit, e2e (83), and agent-core terminate suites green; mixed-batch critical veto no longer leaves the run open for another model turn.
- What was not tested: Multi-hour live Discord/subagent burn against a real hosted model; full gateway session-lane release under load. The mixed-batch agent-loop proof is the acceptance path for terminal behavior without a paid live-model tenant.

## AI disclosure
